review_notes: I read the whole file. I grepped the formal-frontier library and Mathlib for other versions of the objects it defines. The objects are the residue reduction homomorphism on `ULift (Multiplicative (ZMod n))`, the `residueFiniteFunctor`/`residueDiagram` functors, and the residue-to-power-quotient natural isomorphism. The Mathlib hits for `Multiplicative (ZMod n)` were only isolated uses: Coxeter, cyclic-group equivalences, Kummer theory, Selmer groups and roots of unity. I found no Mathlib diagram or inverse system of `ZMod` residue groups, and no residue reduction hom on the ULift multiplicative group. `residueReduction` is a thin wrapper that composes `ZMod.castHom` with `ULift` and `Multiplicative` equivalences. It has its own `id`/`comp` lemmas and is needed to build the functor, so it is a named API rather than a competing concept. Other files in the library (`IntegerPadicResidueLimit`) reuse these declarations and do not redefine them. The comparison with the power-quotient diagram and the limit transport use Mathlib's `NatIso.ofComponents` and `IsLimit.conePointsIsoOfNatIso`. I found no avoidable duplicate of a Mathlib concept. Remaining uncertainty is small: I did not search all of Mathlib for ZMod-indexed diagrams under other names.
